profile.address: The Users Way, Google Berkeley County Data Center, Berkeley County, SC 29461
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Berkeley County, South Carolina data center campus, mapped on The Users Way near Moncks Corner. Google's own South Carolina locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own South Carolina data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the Berkeley County campus opened in 2007 as one of Google's first data centers built in the United States, that the company has invested more than $13 billion in South Carolina since then, and that it generated $7.2 billion in South Carolina economic activity in 2025. Google also cites a 225-megawatt renewable energy purchase agreement signed in 2023, and community programs including longleaf pine and Church Creek watershed restoration and a $1 million Hurricane Helene home-weatherization contribution.

The Berkeley County campus, together with a newer Dorchester County facility opened in 2024, forms Google's South Carolina Lowcountry data center footprint, though Google's own public materials describe the region in aggregate rather than naming individual Berkeley County buildings or per-building capacity figures.

South Carolina's data center sales and use tax exemption, administered by the South Carolina Department of Commerce, applies to qualifying equipment and electricity purchases and has been credited by state officials with helping attract and retain large technology-sector investment in the Lowcountry region, alongside Google's own workforce partnerships with Trident Technical College and Palmetto Goodwill for skilled-trades training.

profile.regional_context: Berkeley County, in South Carolina's Lowcountry near Moncks Corner, was the site of Google's first data center in the state, opened in 2007, and the company has since expanded to a second South Carolina county, Dorchester, with a facility opened in 2024. Santee Cooper and Berkeley Electric Cooperative are among the utilities serving the area. South Carolina offers a state sales and use tax exemption on qualifying data center equipment and electricity, administered by the South Carolina Department of Commerce, that state officials have credited with helping attract and retain large technology-sector investment including Google.

reading.body:
Google does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for this individual facility, only aggregate investment figures at the state level. The Berkeley County campus is one of Google's original long-running US data center sites. A combined $3.3 billion expansion across two South Carolina campuses was announced in September 2024, with a separate $500 million expansion specific to Moncks Corner.

Without published specifications for individual buildings, the capacity and scaling trajectory of this site cannot be assessed from operator disclosures. South Carolina has 14 mapped data center facilities, but only 4 publish power figures, totaling 6.6 MW of disclosed capacity across the state, and this facility does not contribute to that public record.

The absence of published capacity makes it impossible to determine whether this campus is material to AI infrastructure scaling from the facts available. The investment figures suggest Google's continued commitment to the site, but the operational scale and grid impact remain opaque.
